response.title: which power station keeps a wifi router running the longest
response.answer:
For keeping a Wi-Fi router running as long as possible during a power outage, the most important factor is battery capacity (Wh), not the power station's maximum output (W).

A typical Wi-Fi router consumes about 5–20 watts. That means a large portable power station can potentially keep it running for days or even weeks.

One important detail: Using a power station's DC output instead of its AC outlet can significantly extend runtime, because you avoid the energy lost through its AC inverter.

Power stations with the longest router runtime

For a router drawing 10W, here are approximate runtimes with 85% usable battery energy. These are theoretical estimates; AC inverter standby consumption can shorten them substantially.

## Calculate your router's runtime

{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(10)}
{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("1024")}
{@body const [connection,setConnection] = DIL.useState("dc")}
{@body const hours = Number(capacity)*0.85/(watts+(connection==="ac"?8:0))}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      **Router power consumption**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{watts} W</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={5} max={40} step={1} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <label>Battery capacity</label>
    <radio-group direction="col" value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}>
      <radio value="300">300 Wh — small</radio>
      <radio value="1024">1,024 Wh — medium</radio>
      <radio value="2048">2,048 Wh — large</radio>
      <radio value="6144">6,144 Wh — extra large</radio>
    </radio-group>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <label>Connection</label>
    <segmented-control block size="md" value={connection} onChange={setConnection} options={[{"label":"DC output","value":"dc"},{"label":"AC outlet","value":"ac"}]}/>
  </box>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1} align="center">
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated runtime</text>

    <caption>Assumes 85% usable capacity and an illustrative 8W AC standby draw. Actual performance varies by model.</caption>
  </box>
</box>

**My recommendation:** If this is only for a Wi-Fi router, I would start by looking at a 1,000–2,000 Wh station with efficient DC output rather than a massive home-backup battery.

One question: **Are you trying to keep the router running for 24 hours, 3 days, a week, or as long as physically possible regardless of price?** That will change which station I'd recommend.
